topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture framework, learning outcomes, and the concept of cancer hallmarks driving tumor progression.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathways enable cancer cells to achieve growth signal autonomy.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: They illustrate how differentiation arrest contributes to malignant transformation in both hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelial carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations disrupting p53 regulation and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cells regulate replicative lifespan through telomeres and p53-dependent stress pathways, and how cancer cells bypass senescence to achieve immortalization.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways, including aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations that produce oncogenic metabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It discusses the physiological necessity, timing, and molecular regulation of angiogenic signaling required to sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and dynamics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the biological cascade of metastatic dissemination, the role of circulating tumor cells in monitoring, metastatic inefficiency, and the associated genomic features.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It provides a closing synthesis on how cancer hallmarks manifest collectively and concludes the lecture.
